title: Payment Operations Basis: A Payment on an Auto Loan Returned Unpaid
content:
A payment on a loan of the Auto Loans line that the paying bank returns unpaid is reversed in full. Nothing about the reversal is partial.

## What the reversal undoes, part by part

| Part of the returned payment | What the reversal does |
|---|---|
| The part that went to principal | It is restored to principal |
| The part that went to interest | It becomes accrued interest again, because the date of the last payment credited to the loan returns to the date it held before that payment |
| The part that went to charges | That amount becomes due again, as one charge entry of the settlement-reversal kind carrying the returned payment as its source |
| The installment the payment satisfied | It becomes unsatisfied again, so a late charge may follow once the grace days have passed |

## The fee the return carries

The return incurs the returned payment fee the product publishes. Each returned payment carries at most one such fee, of that published amount. Whether a returned payment already carries one is read from the bank's record of charges on the loan, correlated to the returned payment itself.

## Outside this policy

Blocking a payment source after repeated returns is a decision for fraud operations and is not settled here.

## How the two charges stand apart

The reversal does not reach back and cancel the late charge history of the installment; it puts the installment back to unsatisfied, and the ordinary grace days then run from that installment's own due date as they did before. One returned payment therefore produces exactly one returned payment fee, and may in addition produce a late charge on the installment it had satisfied, the two being separate charges on separate grounds.
